beats: The man who conquered half of Europe once ran away from a thousand bunnies!
According to one of his own generals, it happened in the summer of 1806.
Napoleon was at the height of his power, and his court competed to keep him entertained.
His chief of staff, Marshal Berthier, offered a rabbit shoot on his estate just outside Paris.
The estate had everything, except rabbits.
So the marshal bought a thousand of them, and set them loose that very morning.
After a splendid breakfast, the Emperor raised his gun.
But the rabbits didn't run. They bunched up, turned around, and charged straight at Napoleon!
The marshal counter-attacked with a squad of coachmen cracking long whips.
It worked, until the rabbits split into wings, swept around both flanks, and hit the Emperor from behind!
They piled up between his legs until he staggered.
The conqueror of conquerors retreated to his carriage, and left the rabbits the field.
Then the truth came out. The marshal's buyer didn't know one rabbit from another.
He'd bought tame hutch rabbits, not wild ones.
They thought Napoleon was the man with their cabbage, and nobody had fed them that day!
Everyone laughed. The marshal was mortified, because...
